_comment: N-400's OWN entitlement matrix. Scott ruled 2026-09-06: no ContextQuilt
recall for this app.
WHY BOTH context_quilt AND people ARE DISABLED, and this is the whole
point of the file. Disabling context_quilt ALONE does not stop the hook.
chat.py reads `run_hook = state != 'disabled'`, and then, when
context_quilt IS disabled, falls through to:
run_hook = entitlement_state(..., 'people', app) == 'enabled'
which runs the PEOPLE-SCOPED recall lane instead. That lane still calls
hook.before_llm and therefore still resolves _cq_identity(app_id).
AND N-400 HAS NO `cq` ENTRY IN apps.yml, so _cq_identity falls back to
the DEFAULT ShoulderSurf identity. So disabling one feature would have
changed WHICH recall lane ran, not WHETHER GP authenticates to CQ as
ShoulderSurf inside an immigration interview. Both off is what actually
closes it, and the test asserts the closed PROPERTY rather than these
two values.
REPLACE, NOT MERGE: entitlement_matrix() returns the per-app matrix
entirely when present and never merges the flat one. So this file must
carry EVERY feature the flat matrix carries, or the missing ones resolve
'disabled' for N-400 by accident. A test pins that the feature sets
match, so a feature added flat cannot silently go dark here.
Everything else is copied from the flat matrix verbatim and deliberately
unchanged: web_search is live for N-400 and stays live.
